show_output: PC1 ipconfig /all: IPv4 Address: 192.168.10.20; Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0; Default Gateway: 192.168.20.1. R1 show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.10.1 up/up.
expected_fault: PC1 has an incorrect default gateway
expected_fix: Set PC1 gateway to 192.168.10.1 and retest.

symptom_and_context: PC1 is assigned to VLAN 20, but VLAN 20 is absent from the switch VLAN database.
show_output: show vlan brief: VLAN 10 active; VLAN 30 active; VLAN 20 absent. show interfaces Fa0/1 switchport: Administrative Mode: static access; Operational Mode: static access; Access Mode VLAN: 20.
expected_fault: Required VLAN 20 is missing
expected_fix: Create VLAN 20 and verify port membership.

symptom_and_context: Server network 10.20.20.0/24 is behind R2; R1 has no route to it.
show_output: show ip route on R1: 10.20.20.0/24 absent
expected_fault: R1 has no route to the server network
expected_fix: Add the appropriate route and verify connectivity.

symptom_and_context: PC1 and PC2 both use 192.168.10.20/24; connectivity is intermittent.
show_output: show arp: 192.168.10.20 maps to changing MAC addresses
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address exists
expected_fix: Assign unique IP addresses.

symptom_and_context: PC1 cannot reach its gateway because R1 G0/0 is administratively down.
show_output: show ip interface brief: G0/0 administratively down/down
expected_fault: Router interface is administratively shut down
expected_fix: Enable G0/0 and verify connectivity.

symptom_and_context: PC1 is 192.168.10.20/25 while gateway is 192.168.10.129/25; they are in different subnets.
expected_fault: PC1 has an incompatible subnet mask
expected_fix: Correct the subnet mask.

symptom_and_context: PC1 should be in VLAN 10 but Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 20.
show_output: show vlan brief: Fa0/2 in VLAN 20
expected_fault: PC access port is assigned to the wrong VLAN
expected_fix: Assign Fa0/2 to VLAN 10.

symptom_and_context: VLAN 30 exists on both switches, but the inter-switch link is an access port.
show_output: show interfaces Fa0/24 switchport: Administrative Mode: static access; Operational Mode: static access; Access Mode VLAN: 1. show interfaces trunk: Fa0/24 absent.
expected_fault: Inter-switch link is not configured as a trunk
expected_next_command: show interfaces trunk; show interfaces switchport
expected_fix: Configure the link as a trunk.

symptom_and_context: VLAN 40 exists on both switches and the link is trunking, but VLAN 40 is not allowed.
show_output: show interfaces trunk: allowed VLANs 10,20,30; VLAN 40 absent
expected_fault: VLAN 40 is blocked by the trunk allowed list
expected_fix: Allow VLAN 40 on the trunk.

symptom_and_context: PC1 receives an address from the wrong network because the DHCP pool uses 192.168.60.0/24 instead of 192.168.50.0/24.
show_output: PC1 ipconfig /all: IPv4 Address: 192.168.60.20; Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0. Intended client network: 192.168.50.0/24. R1 show run: ip dhcp pool USERS; network 192.168.60.0 255.255.255.0.
expected_fault: DHCP pool is configured for the wrong network
expected_next_command: show ip dhcp pool; show run | section dhcp
expected_fix: Correct the DHCP pool network and renew the lease.

symptom_and_context: The router excludes the entire client subnet, so DHCP has no addresses to allocate.
show_output: R1 show running-config | section ip dhcp: ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL; network 192.168.50.0 255.255.255.0; default-router 192.168.50.1. ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.50.1 192.168.50.254. show ip dhcp pool: Network 192.168.50.0/24; Leased addresses: 0.
expected_fault: DHCP excluded-address range prevents allocation
expected_next_command: show run | section dhcp; show ip dhcp pool
expected_fix: Correct the exclusion range and renew the lease.

symptom_and_context: PC can reach IP addresses but cannot resolve names because its configured DNS server is wrong.
expected_fault: Client uses the wrong DNS server address
expected_fix: Configure the correct DNS server.

symptom_and_context: PC1 can ping Server1 but HTTP access fails because the ACL denies TCP port 80.
show_output: show access-lists: deny tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.20.10 eq 80
expected_fault: ACL blocks HTTP traffic
expected_fix: Modify the ACL according to policy.

topology_note: R1 G0/0 connects to the internal LAN; R1 G0/1 connects to the guest/WAN side.
symptom_and_context: A guest ACL is applied inbound to the internal interface and blocks internal traffic.
show_output: R1 show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.10.1 up/up; G0/1 203.0.113.2 up/up. R1 show running-config: interface G0/0; ip access-group GUEST-FILTER in. interface G0/1; no ip access-group. The GUEST-FILTER ACL is intended for guest traffic, not the internal LAN.
expected_fault: ACL is applied to the wrong interface
expected_fix: Apply the ACL to the correct interface.

topology_note: R1 G0/0 connects to the inside LAN 192.168.10.0/24; R1 G0/1 connects to the outside/WAN.
symptom_and_context: NAT roles are incomplete because the inside interface is not marked as NAT inside.
show_output: R1 show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.10.1 up/up; G0/1 203.0.113.2 up/up. R1 show running-config: interface G0/0 has no ip nat inside; interface G0/1 has ip nat outside. Internal host 192.168.10.20 cannot reach the WAN.
expected_fault: NAT inside designation is missing
expected_next_command: show run interface; show ip nat translations
expected_fix: Configure the correct NAT inside role.

symptom_and_context: Private clients need Internet access but no PAT/NAT overload rule exists.
show_output: R1 show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.10.1 up/up; G0/1 203.0.113.2 up/up. show running-config: interface G0/0 has ip nat inside; interface G0/1 has ip nat outside. ip access-list standard NAT_INSIDE permits 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255. show ip route: 0.0.0.0/0 points to 203.0.113.1. show ip nat translations: <empty> (no active translations). show running-config | include ^ip nat inside source: no matching configuration lines returned; no PAT/overload rule is configured.
expected_fault: NAT overload rule is missing
expected_next_command: show ip nat translations; show run | include ip nat
expected_fix: Configure the required PAT rule.

symptom_and_context: R1 has a route to 10.20.20.0/24, but its next hop is unreachable.
expected_fault: Static route uses an incorrect next hop
expected_next_command: show ip route; show ip interface brief
expected_fix: Correct the next-hop address.

symptom_and_context: OSPF neighbors are established, but the server LAN behind R2 is not advertised.
show_output: R1 show ip ospf neighbor: neighbor 10.0.0.2 is FULL. R1 show ip ospf database: the server LAN 192.168.40.0/24 is absent from the OSPF database. R1 show running-config | section router ospf: router ospf 1; network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.255 area 0. The server LAN interface is not included by any OSPF network statement.
expected_fault: Server LAN is not advertised in OSPF
expected_next_command: show ip ospf database; show run | section router ospf
expected_fix: Advertise the server LAN in OSPF.

symptom_and_context: R1 has internal routes but no default route for unknown destinations.
show_output: show ip route: no Gateway of last resort
expected_fault: Default route is missing
expected_fix: Configure the appropriate default route.

show_output: show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.11.1; PC1 192.168.10.20/24
expected_fault: Router interface has an incorrect IP address
expected_fix: Correct the interface IP address.

symptom_and_context: PC1 is physically connected but Fa0/3 is administratively disabled.
show_output: show interfaces status: Fa0/3 disabled
expected_fault: Switch access interface is shut down
expected_fix: Enable Fa0/3.

symptom_and_context: The trunk is up but native VLANs differ between endpoints.
show_output: show interfaces trunk: SW1 native VLAN 99; SW2 native VLAN 1
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch exists
expected_fix: Configure matching native VLANs.

topology_note: Guest Wi-Fi → AP → SW1 → R1 → Internal Server; VLAN 50 is the guest network and the network policy requires guest-to-internal isolation.
symptom_and_context: Guest clients can reach an internal server; guest VLAN exists but isolation policy is absent.
show_output: show vlan brief: VLAN 50 active. show run: guest VLAN 50 has no ACL/firewall isolation rule permitting only guest Internet access; R1 has no guest-to-internal deny policy. Test: guest client can reach internal server 192.168.10.10.
expected_fault: Guest-to-internal isolation policy is missing
expected_fix: Apply the intended guest isolation policy.

topology_note: Laptop → AP; AP broadcasts CORP-SSID for VLAN 10 and GUEST-SSID for VLAN 50.
symptom_and_context: Laptop connects but receives an internal VLAN address instead of the guest subnet.
show_output: Wireless client status: SSID = CORP-SSID. AP config: CORP-SSID → VLAN 10; GUEST-SSID → VLAN 50. Laptop IP: 192.168.10.25/24. Intended guest subnet: 192.168.50.0/24.
expected_fault: Client is connected to the wrong SSID/network
expected_fix: Connect to the intended SSID and renew DHCP.

symptom_and_context: PC and DHCP server are on different subnets; no DHCP relay is configured.
show_output: show run interface G0/0: no ip helper-address
expected_fault: DHCP relay/helper configuration is missing
expected_next_command: show run interface; show ip interface
expected_fix: Configure the correct DHCP relay.

topology_note: PC1 → SW1 → DNS Server; PC1 is configured to use 192.168.50.10 as its DNS server.
symptom_and_context: PC uses the correct DNS server and can ping it, but DNS queries fail because the DNS service is disabled.
show_output: PC1 ipconfig /all: DNS Server = 192.168.50.10. ping 192.168.50.10 succeeds. nslookup example.local: DNS request timed out. DNS Server service status: Disabled/Stopped.
expected_fault: DNS service is unavailable
expected_fix: Enable/configure DNS service.

topology_note: Replacement PC1 → SW1 Fa0/5; Fa0/5 uses port security with a configured secure MAC address.
symptom_and_context: A replacement PC causes the switch port to enter err-disabled state due to an unexpected MAC.
show_output: show interfaces status: Fa0/5 err-disabled. show port-security interface Fa0/5: Port Security: Enabled; Violation Mode: shutdown; Secure-shutdown VLAN: -; Security Violation Count: 1; Last Source Address: 00AA.BBCC.DDEE.
expected_fault: Port security violation caused err-disabled state
expected_next_command: show port-security interface; show interfaces status
expected_fix: Resolve the MAC/policy issue and recover the port.

topology_note: PC1 → SW1 → SW2 → Server1; SW1 and SW2 have a redundant Layer 2 link, and STP is intentionally used to prevent a loop.
symptom_and_context: A redundant Layer 2 path is blocked by STP to prevent a loop.
show_output: show spanning-tree vlan 10: Fa0/24 is Alternate/Blocking; another path is Forwarding; root bridge and port roles are consistent with the intended redundant topology. Connectivity through the forwarding path succeeds.
expected_fault: STP is blocking the redundant path as designed
expected_fix: Verify the topology; change STP parameters only if required.

topology_note: PC1 → R1 G0/0 → R1 → DHCP Server; the actual DHCP server is 192.168.50.10.
symptom_and_context: DHCP relay points to 192.168.60.10 while the actual DHCP server is 192.168.50.10.
show_output: DHCP Server: 192.168.50.10. show run interface G0/0: ip helper-address 192.168.60.10. The configured helper address does not match the DHCP server address.
expected_fault: DHCP relay points to the wrong server
expected_fix: Correct the helper address.

topology_note: PC1 → R1 → Server1; ACL permits HTTP and DNS, while ICMP is not explicitly permitted.
symptom_and_context: ACL permits HTTP and DNS but not ICMP, so ping fails while application traffic works.
show_output: show access-lists: permit tcp any host 192.168.20.10 eq 80; permit udp any host 192.168.20.10 eq 53; no ICMP permit. Test: HTTP succeeds and DNS succeeds; ping to 192.168.20.10 fails. With no later ICMP permit, the packet reaches the ACL's implicit deny.
expected_fault: ICMP is blocked by the ACL implicit deny
expected_fix: If ping is required by policy, add an appropriate ICMP permit.
